solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor needs to be given purpose

parts.note: tar is an old slang word for a sailor
to get something is to be given it

explanation.surface: A sailor is told he needs to be handed some purpose in life.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or objective one works towards is a synonym for purpose.

clue.text: Leading score is excellent

parts.note: the top one is the leading one
to score is to cut a mark, a notch

explanation.surface: A team's top score is called excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a sports tally or twenty, but it is the mark cut into wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adjective for first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: This may be worn as a favour

definitions.text: This may be worn as a favour

parts.words: This may be worn as a favour
parts.note: a favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge, as at a wedding or election

explanation.surface: Something worn to show support for a cause or person.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour, in the old sense, is a ribbon badge worn to show allegiance, the classic form of which is a rosette.

clue.text: Queen in Belize with hat askew

indicators.note: askew means crooked or out of place, so the letters are set out of order

explanation.surface: A queen visiting Belize wearing her hat at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'askew' rearranges the nine letters of BELIZE and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the name of English queens, most recently Elizabeth II.

clue.text: So, a nicer new storyline

indicators.note: new letters arranged afresh, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone saying a newer, kinder plot is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of SO, A and NICER.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an outline of a plot or sequence of events in a film or play.

clue.text: How a private obstetrician may prefer to be paid?

definitions.text: How a private obstetrician may prefer to be paid?

parts.words: How a private obstetrician may prefer to be paid?
parts.note: a doctor who delivers babies might like payment on each delivery, punning on the retail term for paying when goods arrive

explanation.surface: A question about a private baby doctor's billing preferences.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday shopping phrase for paying when goods are handed over, punning on a doctor delivering a baby.

clue.text: Nymph: Diana, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the given letters

explanation.surface: Suggesting that the goddess Diana might be a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, living in springs and rivers.

clue.text: Backing soldiers, play guitar behind stage

indicators.note: behind places the guitar-playing piece after the soldiers
backing means turning back, so the soldiers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: Musicians backing soldiers, strumming guitars at the back of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Exaggerate about reception

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something
a do is a party or reception

explanation.surface: A warning not to make too much of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo is to take something too far, to exaggerate it.

clue.text: Gambling device, woeful, often her undoing

indicators.note: undoing means taking apart, so the letters are pulled apart and remade

explanation.surface: Gambling, woefully often, brings about a woman's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' rearranges the letters of WOEFUL, OFTEN and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel of fortune is a spinning wheel used in games of chance.

clue.text: Finished with one revolutionary's compositions

parts.note: past means over or finished
I is the Roman numeral for one
Che Guevara is the crossword's usual revolutionary, here possessive

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's compositions are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastiches are artistic works imitating another's style, a kind of composition.

clue.text: Children, a bone of contention

explanation.surface: Children described as a constant source of argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: offspring, and a disputed matter or topic.

clue.text: Scandal revealed before right time

indicators.note: before places the revealed piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A scandal comes to light before the proper moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is public scandal or anger caused by something shocking.

clue.text: Bid organised

definitions.meaning: commanded, as in did as he was bid

explanation.surface: An offer that was put together neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past-tense senses: commanded someone to do something, and put in sequence.

clue.text: Gang, last to leave important railway junction

parts.note: a crew is a gang of workers

indicators.note: last to here means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A gang's last member departing an important railway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a town in Cheshire, England, famous as a major railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire town grew up around one of Britain's busiest railway junctions.

clue.text: Former sweetheart, doll — fame spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former girlfriend, a doll whose fame has spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges the letters of DOLL and FAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an ex-lover, someone once loved.

clue.text: It'll relay changes word for word

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A message relayed through others changes, though it claims to be verbatim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the letters of IT'LL and RELAY (the apostrophe is dropped).
explanation.definitionFit: Literally means exactly, following the original words without interpretation.

clue.text: Blonde he let out, under a moral obligation

indicators.note: let out means freed or loosened, so the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A man let out a blonde woman and now feels he owes her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' rearranges the letters of BLONDE and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indebted, owing something to someone, is the sense here.

clue.text: Just terrible heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: frightful means terrible or dreadful

explanation.surface: A terrible start to a journey being cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful means fair or legitimate, as in a rightful claim, which is just.

clue.text: Progressing on board coach

definitions.meaning: travelling in a railway carriage, aboard a train

explanation.surface: Moving forward while aboard a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus or trainer, but it is a railway carriage here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means under way or in progress, and literally aboard a railway train.

clue.text: Songbird with the French name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, such as a blue tit
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A songbird given a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a name given to a book, work or person.

clue.text: National emblem saint introduced to Leith, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A saint's arrival in Leith causes some strange behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Leith is the port of Edinburgh. 'introduced to' joins ST to LEITH, and 'oddly' rearranges the lot. 'oddly' might suggest alternate letters, but those do not work.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly plant is Scotland's national emblem.

clue.text: Gold found in extensive swamp

indicators.note: found in means the gold sits inside the other piece

parts.note: mass can mean large-scale, as in mass movement
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold discovered in a huge swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or marsh, a synonym of swamp.

clue.text: A month round Connecticut, temperate, no sun

parts.note: O is round in shape
CT is the postal abbreviation for the US state

indicators.note: no means the sun's letter is removed

parts.note: sober means moderate, temperate in drinking
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A month spent in Connecticut with mild weather and no sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the tenth month of the year.

clue.text: Benefit from riding in single-decker outside?

indicators.note: outside means the bus wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a single-decker is a bus with one level
on, as in riding on a horse

explanation.surface: Asking what benefit there is in riding outside a single-deck bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra benefit or payment.

clue.text: Film, extremely short, I got out

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut

parts.note: very means extremely

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A film critic says the film was very short and they left.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a 1958 Hitchcock thriller, an example of a film.

clue.text: A growth on the other hand

parts.note: a gain is an increase or growth

explanation.surface: A growth appears on the other hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can introduce a contrasting point, meaning besides or however.

clue.text: International organisation presented as irrelevant

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
related means told or presented, as a story

explanation.surface: A global body presented as being beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconnected to the matter is irrelevant to it.

clue.text: Knocking back endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: knocking back means reversing, here all the letters that follow
endless means the last letter goes

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: Drinking down a bottle of wine forever is a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like drinking; it reverses RETSIN plus IS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or suggesting evil, the same as ominous.

clue.text: Heraldic beast with very peculiar name

indicators.note: peculiar means strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A heraldic beast bearing a very strange name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a winged two-legged dragon found in heraldry.
